title: Correct shared contacts and CUDA/D3D12 drift
requires: Windows CUDA and D3D12 on the same GPU
scope: Adopt the physics-correctness work started before the lease bootstrap: shared Slang rotational/contact corrections, common static mesh feature classification, and their CUDA/D3D12 numerical compilation contract. Resolve the selected 10/17 comparison failures and shared eight-brick penetration failure. F5-05 and F5-06 remain separate investigation/evidence reviews; this corrective task does not mark those cards complete.
acceptance: All 17 selected same-build CUDA/D3D12 comparisons pass, with zero unsupported cases and unchanged canonical inputs, numerical tolerances and historical goldens.
Both adapters pass the independent eight-brick, four-substep, 300-frame mesh-penetration check against its existing 2 mm limit.
Focused regressions preserve torque-free rotation, floor clearance, closed/open concave seams, two-sided sheets, real boundary-edge impacts and centered fast convex crossings.

D3D12 passes all 13 supported rigid/liquid/cloth gallery scene/reset gates, the 2400-frame hinge/slider fixture, repeated API submissions and resource lifecycle checks with and without validation; the installed gallery survives each supported scene for at least five seconds.

Run the generic domain/coupling lifecycle regressions on CUDA. On D3D12, record their unsupported rope/soft-body/smoke requirements explicitly: skips are not passes or qualification. Do not add new D3D12 domains to complete this correction.

Commit a scoped, revisioned evidence report with reproduction commands, device/toolchain and case hashes. No backend-specific physics fork, tolerance relaxation, full-domain qualification or performance claim.
